title: Geometric semisimplicity of a group-scheme Lie element in a faithful representation
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], let $G$ be a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], and let $X\in\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ be its tangent element at the identity [def-wf-lie-algebra-derivation]. Say that $X$ has a diagonalizable faithful Lie image over $K$ if there are an integer $n\geq1$ and a homomorphism $r:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group] which is a closed subgroup scheme inclusion [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], such that the matrix $dr(X)$ [def-weil-matrix], after applying $k\to K$ entrywise, is conjugate by an invertible matrix over $K$ to a diagonal matrix. Here $dr$ is the differential of the group-scheme homomorphism, read through $\operatorname{Lie}(\operatorname{GL}_{n,k})=\operatorname{Mat}_n(k)$. When $K$ is a fixed algebraic closure of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], this is called geometric semisimplicity of $X$.
